correctness.rationale: An edge with two still-uncovered endpoints has not rung, so exponential memorylessness gives count rates (lambda XY, XZ, YZ)/N. On each fixed time interval the density martingale has quadratic variation O(1/N); the bounded Lipschitz drift and convergence of the three initial densities give uniform convergence in probability. The limiting difference solves (x-y)'=-z(x-y), establishing symmetry even without exact finite-N balance. With p=lambda/2, division gives du/dv=pu/v+1/2. Its integrating factor gives u(v)/v^p=a/c^p+integral from c to v of (1/2)s^(-p) ds; this expression is increasing in v. Since u(t) decreases to zero, the terminal v is the positive root if one exists, and zero otherwise. The integral remains finite at zero only for p<1, where a root exists exactly when c>(2-lambda)a; the equality case gives zero. The logarithm at p=1 and the power at p>1 give the displayed positive endpoints. At time T the terminal total lies between Z_N(T)-X_N(T)-Y_N(T) and Z_N(T)+X_N(T)+Y_N(T); taking N first and T second proves the terminal limit, with boundedness giving convergence in mean. The power exponent at fixed a, its flat exponential endpoint, and the values on K_{3m,3m,4m} follow by substitution. A perfect matching uses m edges between the first two parts and 2m from each to the third. The frozen checker is secondary finite evidence: its two recursions compare the weighted jump chain on 104 small instances, not convergence. It was read, not rerun.
